account:
Today I have repeatedly heard an unusual but very vague claim about a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Townsfolk have repeated it, and the neighbour asked the secretary about it, but nobody I have heard has supplied a specific event or a firsthand account. The secretary explicitly says she has not witnessed a change. I do not yet know whether anything actually changed, who arranged it, or what it is for; repeated wording alone is not confirmation of a plan. The baker might be able to explain, but I did not find him inside the bakery. The secretary later saw him at his market stall. I intend to ask him directly when my appointments allow.

The bridge report I read describes a passable crossing and visible lanterns, not an identified repair need. Its scope excludes concealed structure and load-bearing safety. No repairs or municipal purchases were undertaken under that commission. The secretary has now confirmed that the builder received the agreed two emeralds at 07:58, so there is no outstanding fee. I have no evidence connecting that ordinary inspection with the bakery rumour.

At the scheduled mill inspection I observed two stacks of sixty-four hay bales, removing none. That establishes the visible stock, not anything unusual about its ownership or intended use. I returned the office books after checking my schedule, went home at lunchtime, and have now returned for the one o'clock council letters appointment. The secretary is waiting nearby. Tea with the neighbour at the dockside cottage is at three, followed by office time at 16:30 and home at nineteen. For now the unusual matter is an unexplained rumour, not a demonstrated conspiracy or confirmed public works change.
